        <script id="save-data-connection-testing">
            function hasConnection() {
                return navigator.connection || navigator.mozConnection || navigator.webkitConnection || navigator.msConnection;
            }

            function createLink(src) {
                var preloadLink = document.createElement("link");
                preloadLink.rel = "preload";
                preloadLink.href = src;
                preloadLink.as = "font";
                preloadLink.type = "font/woff2";
                preloadLink.crossOrigin = "";
                document.head.insertBefore(preloadLink, document.head.firstChild);
            }

            var connectionDetail = {
                saveDataEnabled: false,
                slowConnection: false
            };

            var connection = hasConnection();
            if (connection) {
                connectionDetail.saveDataEnabled = connection.saveData;
                if (/\slow-2g|2g/.test(connection.effectiveType)) {
                    connectionDetail.slowConnection = true;
                }
            }

            if (!(connectionDetail.saveDataEnabled || connectionDetail.slowConnection)) {
                createLink("/oscar-static/fonts/HardingText-Regular-Web-cecd90984f.woff2");
            } else {
                document.documentElement.classList.add('save-data');
            }
        </script>

        if ( typeof window.CustomEvent === "function" ) return false;
        function CustomEvent ( event, params ) {
            params = params || { bubbles: false, cancelable: false, detail: null };
            var evt = document.createEvent( 'CustomEvent' );
            evt.initCustomEvent( event, params.bubbles, params.cancelable, params.detail );
            return evt;
        }

        CustomEvent.prototype = window.Event.prototype;

    })();

                e.setAttribute('data-consent', h);
            }
            s.insertAdjacentElement('afterend', e);
        }
        cc();
    })(window,document,'script');
</script>

                ].filter(function (s) {
                    if (s.src === null) return false;
                    if (moduleSupport && s.nomodule) return false;
                    return !(!moduleSupport && s.module);
                }),

                register: function (value) {
                    this.registered.push(value);
                },

                ready: function () {
                    if (this.registered.length === this.scripts.length) {
                        this.registered.forEach(function (fn) {
                            if (typeof fn === 'function') {
                                setTimeout(fn, 0); 
                            }
                        });
                        this.ready = function () {};
                    }
                },

                insert: function (s) {
                    var t = d.getElementById('js-position' + this.index);
                    if (t && t.insertAdjacentElement) {
                        t.insertAdjacentElement('afterend', s);
                    } else {
                        d.head.appendChild(s);
                    }
                    ++this.index;
                },

                createScript: function (script, beforeLoad) {
                    var s = d.createElement('script');
                    s.id = 'js-position' + (this.index + 1);
                    s.setAttribute('data-test', script.test);
                    if (beforeLoad) {
                        s.defer = 'defer';
                        s.onload = function () {
                            if (script.noinit) {
                                loader.register(true);
                            }
                            if (d.readyState === 'interactive' || d.readyState === 'complete') {
                                loader.ready();
                            }
                        };
                    } else {
                        s.async = 'async';
                    }
                    s.src = script.src;
                    return s;
                },

                init: function () {
                    this.scripts.forEach(function (s) {
                        loader.insert(loader.createScript(s, true));
                    });

                    d.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
                        loader.ready();

    <script type="application/ld+json">{"mainEntity":{"headline":"Multimodal pooled Perturb-CITE-seq screens in patient models define mechanisms of cancer immune evasion","description":"Resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is a key challenge in cancer therapy. To elucidate underlying mechanisms, we developed Perturb-CITE-sequencing (Perturb-CITE-seq), enabling pooled clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)–Cas9 perturbations with single-cell transcriptome and protein readouts. In patient-derived melanoma cells and autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) co-cultures, we profiled transcriptomes and 20 proteins in ~218,000 cells under ~750 perturbations associated with cancer cell-intrinsic ICI resistance (ICR). We recover known mechanisms of resistance, including defects in the interferon-γ (IFN-γ)–JAK/STAT and antigen-presentation pathways in RNA, protein and perturbation space, and new ones, including loss/downregulation of CD58. Loss of CD58 conferred immune evasion in multiple co-culture models and was downregulated in tumors of melanoma patients with ICR. CD58 protein expression was not induced by IFN-γ signaling, and CD58 loss conferred immune evasion without compromising major histocompatibility complex (MHC) expression, suggesting that it acts orthogonally to known mechanisms of ICR. This work provides a framework for the deciphering of complex mechanisms by large-scale perturbation screens with multimodal, single-cell readouts, and discovers potentially clinically relevant mechanisms of immune evasion. To elucidate underlying mechanisms, we developed Perturb-CITE-sequencing (Perturb-CITE-seq), enabling pooled clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)&#8211;Cas9 perturbations with single-cell transcriptome and protein readouts. In patient-derived melanoma cells and autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) co-cultures, we profiled transcriptomes and 20&#8201;proteins in ~218,000&#8201;cells under ~750&#8201;perturbations associated with cancer cell-intrinsic ICI resistance (ICR). CD58 protein expression was not induced by IFN-&#947; signaling, and CD58 loss conferred immune evasion without compromising major histocompatibility complex (MHC) expression, suggesting that it acts orthogonally to known mechanisms of ICR. This work provides a framework for the deciphering of complex mechanisms by large-scale perturbation screens with multimodal, single-cell readouts, and discovers potentially clinically relevant mechanisms of immune evasion. Pooled CRISPR perturbation screens with multimodal RNA and protein single-cell profiling readout (Perturb-CITE-seq) applied to patient-derived melanoma and tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte co-cultures identifies new tumor immune evasion mechanisms."/>

                <div class="c-article-body">
                    <section aria-labelledby="Abs1" data-title="Abstract" lang="en"><div class="c-article-section" id="Abs1-section"><h2 class="c-article-section__title js-section-title js-c-reading-companion-sections-item" id="Abs1">Abstract</h2><div class="c-article-section__content" id="Abs1-content"><p>Resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is a key challenge in cancer therapy. To elucidate underlying mechanisms, we developed Perturb-CITE-sequencing (Perturb-CITE-seq), enabling pooled clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)–Cas9 perturbations with single-cell transcriptome and protein readouts. In patient-derived melanoma cells and autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) co-cultures, we profiled transcriptomes and 20 proteins in ~218,000 cells under ~750 perturbations associated with cancer cell-intrinsic ICI resistance (ICR). We recover known mechanisms of resistance, including defects in the interferon-γ (IFN-γ)–JAK/STAT and antigen-presentation pathways in RNA, protein and perturbation space, and new ones, including loss/downregulation of <i>CD58</i>. Loss of <i>CD58</i> conferred immune evasion in multiple co-culture models and was downregulated in tumors of melanoma patients with ICR. CD58 protein expression was not induced by IFN-γ signaling, and <i>CD58</i> loss conferred immune evasion without compromising major histocompatibility complex (MHC) expression, suggesting that it acts orthogonally to known mechanisms of ICR. This work provides a framework for the deciphering of complex mechanisms by large-scale perturbation screens with multimodal, single-cell readouts, and discovers potentially clinically relevant mechanisms of immune evasion.</p></div></div></section>

                        <section data-title="Data availability"><div class="c-article-section" id="data-availability-section"><h2 class="c-article-section__title js-section-title js-c-reading-companion-sections-item" id="data-availability">Data availability</h2><div class="c-article-section__content" id="data-availability-content">
              
              <p>Processed data are available via the single-cell portal: <a href="https://singlecell.broadinstitute.org/single_cell/study/SCP1064/multi-modal-pooled-perturb-cite-seq-screens-in-patient-models-define-novel-mechanisms-of-cancer-immune-evasion">https://singlecell.broadinstitute.org/single_cell/study/SCP1064/multi-modal-pooled-perturb-cite-seq-screens-in-patient-models-define-novel-mechanisms-of-cancer-immune-evasion</a>. Raw data are available on the Broad Data Use and Oversight System through the accession code DUOS-000124: <a href="https://duos.broadinstitute.org">https://duos.broadinstitute.org</a>.</p>

                <h3 class="c-article__sub-heading" id="FPar3">Competing interests</h3>
                <p>A. Regev is a cofounder and equity holder of Celsius Therapeutics, an equity holder in Immunitas and, until 31 July 2020, was an SAB member of Thermo Fisher Scientific, Syros Pharmaceuticals, Neogene Therapeutics and Asimov. From 1 August 2020, A. Regev has been an employee of Genentech. B.I. is a consultant for Merck and Volastra Therapeutics. B.E.J. is on the scientific advisory board of Checkpoint Therapeutics. From 16 November 2020, K.G.S. and O.R.-R. have been employees of Genentech. A. Rotem is a consultant to eGenesis, a SAB member of NucleAI and an equity holder in Celsius Therapeutics. Since 31 August 2020, A. Rotem has been an employee of AstraZeneca. K.W.W. serves on the scientific advisory board of TCR2 Therapeutics, T-Scan Therapeutics, SQZ Biotech and Nextechinvest and receives sponsored research funding from Novartis. K.W.W. is a cofounder of Immunitas, a biotech company. These activities are not related to the research reported in this publication. C.B. is on the scientific advisory board of Myst Therapeutics. A. Regev, B.I., J.C.M., K.R.G.-S., P.I.T. and C.J.F. are inventors on a patent application related to this work.</p>

Plates were imaged at 0, 24, 48 and 72 hours, and viable cell counts were normalized to starting counts to quantify outgrowth of target cells. <b>b</b>-<b>d</b>, Sorting and gating strategy to isolate and expand TIL cultures prior to co-culture. b. TILs grown in IL2 or OKT3-stimulated for 72 hours and analyzed after 4 hours of PMA-I-stimulation. FMO, fluorescent-minus-one control b. TILs from 2686 retain ability to induce IFNγ and TNFa, and OKT-3 reactivation leads to an increase in Granzyme-B production compared to TILs grown in IL2 alone. <b>c</b>, MaMel-134 TILs produce IFNγ, TNFa, and Granzyme-B. <b>d</b>, MaMel-80 TILs produce IFNγ, TNFa, and Granzyme-B. e-h. Impact of time, dose, IFNγ pre-treatment, MHC-I blocking, and OKT3 on TIL-mediated killing in the co-culture system from patient 2686. Ratio of viable cancer cells (y axis, relative to t0) in co-cultures: (<b>e</b>) after different time points of co-culture at increasing TIL:cancer cell ratios (x axis), where TILs were restimulated with immobilized OKT3 for 72 h prior to co-culture; <b>f</b>, after 48 h of co-culture, where cancer cells were pre-treated with 1 ng/ml IFNγ for 16 hours (without prior OKT3-reactivation); <b>g</b>, after 48 hours of co-culture as in (<b>f</b>) but using OKT3-reactivated TILs. <b>h</b>, Specificity of IFNγ pre-treatment approach. Ratio of viable allogenic cancer cells (y axis, relative to t0) in different culture conditions with or without IFNγ pre-treatment (x axis) grown from 0 to 72 hours (color bars) with 2686 TILs with or without prior reactivation with OKT3. For <b>e</b>-<b>h</b>, we performed a one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc test. Error bars: Mean±SD. All experiments were performed in triplicates in each of at least two independent experiments.</p></div></div><div class="c-article-supplementary__item js-c-reading-companion-figures-item" data-test="supp-item" id="Fig7"><h3 class="c-article-supplementary__title u-h3"><a data-test="supp-info-link" class="print-link" data-track="call_to_action" data-track-action="view supplementary info" data-track-context="Extended data" data-track-label="extended data fig. 2 generation of cas9 transgenic" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1/figures/7" data-supp-info-image="//media.springernature.com/lw685/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-021-00779-1/MediaObjects/41588_2021_779_Fig7_ESM.jpg">Extended Data Fig. 2 Generation of Cas9 transgenic patient derived lines and sgDNA library titration.</a></h3><div class="c-article-supplementary__description" data-component="thumbnail-container"><p><b>a</b>, High Cas9 activity in Cas9 transgenic line. Flow cytometry of EGFP levels in Cas9-expressing and parental melanoma cells from patient 2686 transduced with lentivirus encoding EGFP and an EGFP targeting sgRNA at MOI &lt;1 and selected using puromycin. <b>b-d</b>, Transduction of sgDNA lentiviral library to Cas9 transgenic line. <b>b</b>, Proportion of mKATE2+ cells prior to selection (x axis) and survival after puromycin selection (y axis) in 2686 melanoma Cas9 transgenic cells transduced with the ICR library. Line: Linear regression, Pearson R2=0.90. <b>c</b>, Percentage of mKate2+ cells (y axis) in 2686 melanoma Cas9 transgenic cells transduced with the ICR library at virus dilutions (x axis). Red: Dilution used for the Perturb-CITE-seq screen. d. Proportion of cells estimated to be infected by one virus (y axis) at different dilutions of the ICR library (x axis). Red: Dilution used for the Perturb-CITE-seq screen.</p></div></div><div class="c-article-supplementary__item js-c-reading-companion-figures-item" data-test="supp-item" id="Fig8"><h3 class="c-article-supplementary__title u-h3"><a data-test="supp-info-link" class="print-link" data-track="call_to_action" data-track-action="view supplementary info" data-track-context="Extended data" data-track-label="extended data fig. 3 crispr/cas9 viability screen " href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1/figures/8" data-supp-info-image="//media.springernature.com/lw685/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-021-00779-1/MediaObjects/41588_2021_779_Fig8_ESM.jpg">Extended Data Fig. 3 CRISPR/Cas9 viability screen in the co-culture system.</a></h3><div class="c-article-supplementary__description" data-component="thumbnail-container"><p><b>a</b>, Dose-response killing in the co-culture experiment validates target killing range. Percent of surviving cells relative to IFNγ pretreated target cells (y axis) in different co-culture conditions (x axis) from a plate run in parallel to the viability and Perturb-CITE screens, with triplicate wells for each condition. One-way ANOVA with Dunnet post-hoc test. Error bars: Mean±SD. <b>b</b>,<b>c</b>, Screen reproducibility across triplicates. Number of reads detected (x, y axis) for each sgDNA (dots) when comparing each pair within triplicate experiments (color legend) in pre-treated day 7 (<b>b</b>) or day 14 (<b>c</b>). Pearson correlation coefficients are noted in the color legend. <b>d-f</b>, Identification of essential genes and genes affecting resistance to TIL mediated killing. Relative depletion (log2(FC), x axis) for each individual sgDNA (red bar) of the top20 target genes by MAGeCK analysis (rows) (n = 3 sgDNAs/target gene, <a data-track="click" data-track-label="link" data-track-action="section anchor" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#Sec11">Methods</a>) on day 7 (without TILs, to recover essential genes, <b>d</b>), day 17 of 2:1 TIL:cancer cells co-cultures, comparing control cells (<b>e</b>), or day 17 of IFNγ treated cells (<b>f</b>, no co-culture). Bold lettering indicates significantly enriched / depleted target.</p></div></div><div class="c-article-supplementary__item js-c-reading-companion-figures-item" data-test="supp-item" id="Fig9"><h3 class="c-article-supplementary__title u-h3"><a data-test="supp-info-link" class="print-link" data-track="call_to_action" data-track-action="view supplementary info" data-track-context="Extended data" data-track-label="extended data fig. 4 characterization of different" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1/figures/9" data-supp-info-image="//media.springernature.com/lw685/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-021-00779-1/MediaObjects/41588_2021_779_Fig9_ESM.jpg">Extended Data Fig. 4 Characterization of different immune pressures by single-cell RNA and protein profiles.</a></h3><div class="c-article-supplementary__description" data-component="thumbnail-container"><p><b>a</b>,<b>b</b>, Removal of profiled T cells. a. UMAP embedding of single cell RNA-Seq profiles from the Perturb-CITE-seq screen, colored by unsupervised cluster assignment<sup><a data-track="click" data-track-action="reference anchor" data-track-label="link" data-test="citation-ref" aria-label="Reference 34" title="Wolf, F. A., Angerer, P. &amp; Theis, F. J. SCANPY: large-scale single-cell gene expression data analysis. Genome Biol. 19, 15 (2018)." href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#ref-CR34" id="ref-link-section-d50600613e3495">34</a></sup> (<a data-track="click" data-track-label="link" data-track-action="section anchor" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#Sec11">Methods</a>). <b>b</b>, A permutation test was used to score marker genes associated with each cluster shown in (<b>a</b>)<sup><a data-track="click" data-track-action="reference anchor" data-track-label="link" data-test="citation-ref" aria-label="Reference 35" title="Pedregosa, F. et al. Scikit-learn: machine learning in Python. J. Mach. Learn. Res. 12, 2825–2830 (2011)." href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#ref-CR35" id="ref-link-section-d50600613e3509">35</a></sup>. Score (y axis, permutation test, <a data-track="click" data-track-label="link" data-track-action="section anchor" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#Sec11">Methods</a>) of marker genes (x axis) associated with the distinct cluster marked by an arrow in (<b>a</b>), include canonical T cell markers. <b>c</b>, Cell complexity affects scRNA-Seq profiles. UMAP embedding of scRNA-Seq profiles of cancer cells only, colored by UMI count bins. <b>d</b>,<b>e</b>, CITE profiles of 20 cell surface proteins do not reflect cell cycle phases (<b>d</b>) or UMI count (<b>e</b>). UMAP embedding of cells (dots) by CITE-seq profiles (dots) colored by cell cycle phase, as scored from scRNA-Seq of the cells, and (<b>e</b>) UMAP of cells by count bins (indicated in legend). <b>f-h</b>, Limited relation between the cell cycle and immune pressure or phenotype. UMAP embedding of cells (dots) based only on RNA expression on cell cycle genes colored by (<b>f</b>) cell cycle phase based on the cell’s RNA profile; (<b>g</b>) MHC protein levels from the CITE signal of the cell; or (<b>h</b>) condition.</p></div></div><div class="c-article-supplementary__item js-c-reading-companion-figures-item" data-test="supp-item" id="Fig10"><h3 class="c-article-supplementary__title u-h3"><a data-test="supp-info-link" class="print-link" data-track="call_to_action" data-track-action="view supplementary info" data-track-context="Extended data" data-track-label="extended data fig. 5 learning expression programs " href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1/figures/10" data-supp-info-image="//media.springernature.com/lw685/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-021-00779-1/MediaObjects/41588_2021_779_Fig10_ESM.jpg">Extended Data Fig. 5 Learning expression programs in different conditions.</a></h3><div class="c-article-supplementary__description" data-component="thumbnail-container"><p><b>a-f</b>, Identification of programs by jackstraw PCA in each condition. a-c. Explained variance (y axis) by each principal component (x axis) for PCA performed on control (<b>a</b>), IFNγ-treated (<b>b</b>), or co-culture (<b>c</b>) Perturb-CITE-seq data. <b>d-f</b>, Number of features (y axis) for each jackstraw program (x axis) for models learned on control (<b>a</b>), IFNγ-treated (<b>b</b>), or co-culture (<b>c</b>) Perturb-CITE-seq data. Dotted red line: cutoff for programs considered in further analysis. <b>g</b>, G2M program learned from control dataset. UMAP embedding of cells (dots) by scRNA-seq profiles, with cells colored by the gene set score (color bar) (<a data-track="click" data-track-label="link" data-track-action="section anchor" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#Sec11">Methods</a>) of a G2M cell cycle control program (compare to Fig. <a data-track="click" data-track-label="link" data-track-action="figure anchor" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#Fig3">3f</a>) (<a data-track="click" data-track-label="link" data-track-action="section anchor" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#Sec11">Methods</a>). <b>h</b>, Identifying related programs across conditions. Jaccard index (color bar) for each pair of programs across all 30 programs (rows).</p></div></div><div class="c-article-supplementary__item js-c-reading-companion-figures-item" data-test="supp-item" id="Fig11"><h3 class="c-article-supplementary__title u-h3"><a data-test="supp-info-link" class="print-link" data-track="call_to_action" data-track-action="view supplementary info" data-track-context="Extended data" data-track-label="extended data fig. 6 addressing cell cycle and com" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1/figures/11" data-supp-info-image="//media.springernature.com/lw685/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-021-00779-1/MediaObjects/41588_2021_779_Fig11_ESM.jpg">Extended Data Fig. 6 Addressing cell cycle and complexity covariates by the Perturb-CITE-seq model and impact of targeting vs. non-targeting guides.</a></h3><div class="c-article-supplementary__description" data-component="thumbnail-container"><p><b>a</b>, Estimated Multiplicity of infection (MOI). Distribution of cells (%, y axis) at different estimated MOI (x axis) in each experimental condition (color legend) as determined from the guide dictionary (<a data-track="click" data-track-label="link" data-track-action="section anchor" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#Sec11">Methods</a>). <b>b</b>,<b>c</b>, Improved model fit following accounting for cell state as a covariate. Pearson correlation (color bar) between the residuals from the linear model fit for each regulated feature (columns) from models learned without (<b>b</b>) or with (<b>c</b>) cell state covariates accounting for the cell cycle and cell complexity.</p></div></div><div class="c-article-supplementary__item js-c-reading-companion-figures-item" data-test="supp-item" id="Fig12"><h3 class="c-article-supplementary__title u-h3"><a data-test="supp-info-link" class="print-link" data-track="call_to_action" data-track-action="view supplementary info" data-track-context="Extended data" data-track-label="extended data fig. 7 role of cd58 in resistance to" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1/figures/12" data-supp-info-image="//media.springernature.com/lw685/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-021-00779-1/MediaObjects/41588_2021_779_Fig12_ESM.jpg">Extended Data Fig. 7 Role of CD58 in resistance to T cell mediated killing and regulation of PD-L1.</a></h3><div class="c-article-supplementary__description" data-component="thumbnail-container"><p><b>a</b>, Validation of CRISPR/Cas9 KO (and unperturbed control) melanoma cells. <b>a</b>, Distribution of fluorescent intensity of CD58 (APC-CD58), B2M (APC-B2M), MHC-I (FITC-HLA-A,B,C), PD-L1 (APC-CD274) or staining with isotype control, without or with IFNg stimulation, in 2686 melanoma cells. <b>b</b>, Validation of <i>CD58</i> KO MaMel-134, and <b>c</b>, MaMel-80 melanoma cells. <b>d</b>, Comparable growth of control and KO cells. Ratio of viable cells relative to timepoint 0 (y axis) for control and <i>B2M</i> KO, <i>CD58</i> KO or <i>CD274</i> KO melanoma cells from patient 2686 (x axis). <b>e</b>, Comparable induction of apoptosis in response to Staurosporin and resistance to DTIC in control and KO melanoma cells. Percent of cells inducing Caspase 3/7 (y axis) in control and <i>B2M</i> KO, <i>CD58</i> KO or <i>CD274</i> KO melanoma cells (color code) from patient 2686 in different treatment conditions (x axis). <b>f</b>, Co-culture experiments of three melanoma cells lines (2686, MaMel134 and MaMel80) at increasing ratios of NK cells and tumor cells with different genotypes (including <i>CD58</i> KO, <i>B2M</i> KO in all models, and additionally <i>CD274</i> KO in 2686). <b>g-j</b>, <i>CD58</i> perturbation in co-culture does not affect <i>B2M</i> and <i>HLA</i> expression at the RNA and protein level but induces <i>CD274</i>. Distribution of fluorescent intensity by flow cytometry (corresponding to Fig. <a data-track="click" data-track-label="link" data-track-action="figure anchor" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1#Fig5">5i-k</a>) of MHC Class I and II, CD58, and PD-L1 in parental (control) and <i>CD58</i> KO lines at baseline (<b>g</b>) and after 72 hours of stimulation with either 1 ng IFNγ (<b>h</b>) or 10 ng IFNγ (<b>i</b>), and summary of the impact of IFNγ on CD58 protein abundance after 72 hours. In all experiments, we used a one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc test. Error bars: Mean ±SD. All experiments were performed in triplicates in each of at least two independent experiments.</p></div></div><div class="c-article-supplementary__item js-c-reading-companion-figures-item" data-test="supp-item" id="Fig13"><h3 class="c-article-supplementary__title u-h3"><a data-test="supp-info-link" class="print-link" data-track="call_to_action" data-track-action="view supplementary info" data-track-context="Extended data" data-track-label="extended data fig. 8 known mechanisms of immune ev" href="/articles/s41588-021-00779-1/figures/13" data-supp-info-image="//media.springernature.com/lw685/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-021-00779-1/MediaObjects/41588_2021_779_Fig13_ESM.jpg">Extended Data Fig. 8 Known mechanisms of immune evasion and distinct role of CD58.</a></h3><div class="c-article-supplementary__description" data-component="thumbnail-container"><p><b>a</b>, Schematic representation of interactions between T cell and cancer cells. At baseline, TCR stimulation via peptide-loaded MHC Class I and through CD58:CD2 co-stimulation results in production of cytokines (such as IFNγ, Granzymes), which lead to activation of the IFNγ-JAK/STAT-pathway that determine the cell fate and expression of surface proteins. <b>b</b>, In the absence of antigen presentation, either due to genetic defects or downregulation of the antigen presentation machinery, cancer cells survive. <b>c</b>, Defects in the JAK/STAT-pathway (such as deleterious mutations in JAK genes) result in poor response of cancer cells to T cell secreted IFNγ and promote cancer cell survival. <b>d</b>, Loss or downregulation of CD58 does not interfere with antigen presentation or JAK/STAT-signaling per se, but reduces T cell co-stimulation while simultaneously promoting increased co-inhibitory signaling via PD-L1, and therefore overall confers resistance to T cell mediated killing.</p></div></div></div></div></div></section><section
